purpose.summary: Link a default-off, local-regtest-only volatile block observer into the standalone node without adding an index or changing consensus.
scope: Ask one falsifiable question: can a compiled-in but runtime-disabled observer preserve legacy node behavior, while explicit local-regtest opt-in observes exact block connect and disconnect order without becoming authoritative?
Add BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER with compile-time default OFF; the OFF build neither enters Chronik nor discovers Rust/Cargo, exposes the runtime flag, or links observer symbols.
When compiled in, keep runtime default OFF and require explicit -chronikobserver on the exact CBaseChainParams::REGTEST identity.
Bridge serialized validation-interface block callbacks to a dependency-free Rust static library that owns only volatile sequence and fingerprint state.
Drain the validation callback queue before unregistering the C++ adapter and destroying its opaque Rust handle.
Prove the enabled boundary with two blocks, invalidate/reconsider, exact six-event ordering, an independent fingerprint oracle, network-profile rejection, and absence of Chronik files or sockets.
exclusions: No transaction payload, mempool event, SLP, ALP, or CashTokens classification reaches the observer.
No database, file, socket, API, service, Rust thread, persistence, restart reconstruction, reindex, pruning, or deep-reorganization index behavior is added.
No callback result can accept, reject, reorder, or select a block, transaction, or chain.
No consensus, chain parameter, activation, testnet, mainnet, P2P, RPC, wallet, or user-interface behavior changes.
No local binary, build cache, raw output, absolute host path, parent environment, operator material, private history, or unrelated product material enters this change.

Locally detects the compiled component and checks disabled then enabled execution, exact six-event ordering and fingerprints, no Chronik path/socket, and rejection on main, testnet, testnet4, and scalenet.

commands: Fresh-configure and build bitcoind with BUILD_CHRONIK_BUILD_ONLY=OFF and BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=OFF, then run symbol, option, and mining_basic checks.
expected_results: CMake does not discover Rust/Cargo, no observer symbol or option exists, -chronikobserver is rejected as unknown, and legacy mining passes.

commands: Fresh-configure and build bitcoind with BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=ON, inspect the final executable, launch without -chronikobserver, and run mining_basic.
expected_results: The final executable contains all four Rust C-ABI symbols; runtime launches register no observer or Chronik state by default; legacy mining passes.

commands: Run feature_chronik_block_observer.py against the compiled-in build on a fresh isolated regtest datadir.
expected_results: The volatile observer precursor passes exact connect/disconnect diagnostics, but no index or local-regtest-indexing completion claim is emitted.

scenarios.command: Run feature_chronik_block_observer.py with the compiled-in build: first runtime disabled, then explicit regtest opt-in, then non-regtest rejection probes.
expected_results: Disabled execution emits no Chronik event; enabled regtest emits exact sequence 1..6 for connect, connect, disconnect, disconnect, reconnect, reconnect; independent fingerprints match; shutdown reports six; no Chronik file or socket exists; main, testnet, testnet4, and scalenet reject opt-in.
failure_conditions: Any enabled non-regtest launch, event-order or fingerprint mismatch, missing callback drain, Chronik path/socket, validation decision, or claim of index reconstruction fails the scenario.

platforms: Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 public verification after technical acceptance

limitations: This change observes only block hash, height, and connection direction; it is not an index and receives no transaction payload.
Volatile state resets at shutdown and cannot prove restart, full reindex, chainstate reindex, pruning, or deep-reorganization reconstruction.

The local macOS final binaries required an untracked Boost 1.90 compatibility include because unchanged legacy code calls removed boost::filesystem::basename; those binaries are diagnostic only and never evidence artifacts.
The committed lockfile fixes registry versions and checksums but does not lock the compiler, operating-system image, native toolchain, or final binaries.
A fresh Cargo cache requires one online population step before governed offline builds.
Local tests are contradiction checks only; no result is public reproduction evidence at record-review time.
counterevidence: No public build or functional execution of the exact candidate exists at record-review time.
Exact event diagnostics do not demonstrate durable indexing, complete chain state, native-asset parsing, token validity, or API compatibility.
Five required optional-indexing scenarios remain deliberately unimplemented and Open Question.
